cues.speaker: Maya
cues.text: Welcome to The Signal. Today we explore the long history of Madame Tussauds.

cues.speaker: Daniel
cues.text: Founded in London in 1835 by Marie Tussaud, it became a major tourist attraction during the Victorian era.

cues.speaker: Maya
cues.text: Marie Tussaud was born Marie Grosholtz in 1761 in Strasbourg, France.

cues.speaker: Daniel
cues.text: She learned wax modeling from her mother's employer, Philippe Curtius, before creating her first sculpture of Voltaire in 1777.

cues.speaker: Maya
cues.text: The original museum opened in Baker Street in 1835, featuring the famous Chamber of Horrors.

cues.speaker: Daniel
cues.text: Space limitations there led her grandson to commission a new building on Marylebone Road, which opened in 1884.

cues.speaker: Maya
cues.text: The museum expanded globally, with its first overseas branch opening in Amsterdam in 1970.

cues.speaker: Daniel
cues.text: It was later acquired by Merlin Entertainments in 2007 and now has locations across four continents.

cues.speaker: Maya
cues.text: That is the story of the world's most famous wax museum.
